page: Microsoft Azure A2_v2 is an entry-level virtual machine belonging to the Av2 server family. It is equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an Intel Xeon 8171M processor running at 2.6 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 2 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core, 4.0 GB of system memory providing 2.0 GB per core, and 20 GB of local storage. The CPU architecture is x86_64, featuring a cache hierarchy of 32 KB L1d, 0.25 MB L2, and 50 MB L3 cache. It supports hardware-assisted virtualization via Microsoft Hyper-V and includes CPU flags such as AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA.

Benchmark evaluations place the A2_v2 in the bottom 10% across all tested performance categories. Single-core and multi-core CPU tests, including stress-ng and Geekbench, demonstrate poor processing capabilities. Memory bandwidth is also limited, with read-only cached small block speeds at 60.11 GB/sec and uncached large block read speeds at 7.64 GB/sec. Data processing tasks, such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression, show low throughput. Database operations and web serving capabilities are constrained, with Redis SET operations reaching 0.95 million operations per second and static web serving throughput limited to 0.82 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the A2_v2 offers a low-cost entry point for basic computing needs, but its low resource density and poor benchmark-per-resource tradeoffs make it unsuitable for performance-critical tasks. Given the lack of a GPU and the limited memory and CPU performance, this server is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic development, testing environments, low-traffic web serving, or simple administrative scripting where performance is not a primary requirement.
